editorial:
Imagine a world where something as simple as stolen milk can throw a whole city into a panic. You get to follow Susan Anspach, who plays a determined news reporter trying to get to the bottom of why milk and gas prices are suddenly skyrocketing. It starts as a weird little investigation, but things quickly spiral out of control. The vibe is very typical of early 80s comedies, where a small misunderstanding grows into a giant mess. You will find yourself rooting for the reporter as she gets pulled into a web of strange characters and chaotic situations that feel like a wild ride.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the characters and the way the tension builds toward a massive car chase. While the pacing starts a bit slow, the payoff is worth it for the laughs and the action. If you enjoy quirky plots and retro charm, you should definitely check this one out. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you want the best picture. Better yet, grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection so you can watch it whenever you want.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a chaotic multiple car chase that brings all the different characters together in one place. After all the confusion over the stolen milk and the price hikes, the truth comes out about who was actually manipulating the market. The reporter finally gets her big story, the bad guys are caught in the wreckage, and the madness settles down. It ends on a light note, showing that the chaos was all over a few gallons of milk.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s comedies and crime capers.
